event.description: Share QKV transform across depth and widen feed-forward paths
event.proposal: Family: parameter tying. Current retained frontier is 3,040 parameters at 99.850000%, a +0.850000 percentage-point margin over 99%. There have been 0 prior attempts in this family, so there is no accepted or failed in-family result. The most recent experiment, attempt-0025 in position representation, was a scored nonqualification at 32.44%, while attempt-0022 remains retained. Hypothesis: both blocks can reuse one 16x48 QKV transform because their inputs, normalizers, attention maps, residual states, and feed-forward paths remain layer-specific; widening each feed-forward path from 10 to 16 reallocates 384 of the 768 saved parameters. The resulting 2,656-parameter model is a genuine parameter-sharing architecture. This is more informative than the nearest untested tying alternative, sharing the feed-forward matrices, because QKV sharing saves more capacity while retaining independent nonlinear computation in each block.
